topics.title: Docker Concepts
topics.description: The five nouns every Docker question is built on, plus the classic container-versus-VM distinction.

rows: Image
Immutable, layered filesystem plus metadata (the recipe)
Container
Running instance of an image with isolated process, network, and filesystem (namespaces + cgroups, not a VM, shares the host kernel)
Layer
Each Dockerfile instruction; cached and shared between images
Registry
Image storage (Docker Hub, ECR, Harbor); push and pull by tag
Volume
Persistent data outside the container writable layer

topics.containersVsVirtualMachines: Containers share the host kernel and isolate at the process level, so they start in milliseconds with megabytes of overhead. VMs virtualize hardware with a full guest OS, giving stronger isolation at a much heavier cost.

topics.title: Dockerfile
topics.description: The multi-stage Spring Boot Dockerfile to know cold.

dockerfile.title: Dockerfile (Spring Boot, multi-stage)
dockerfile.code:
# ---- build stage ----
FROM eclipse-temurin:21-jdk AS build
WORKDIR /app
COPY mvnw pom.xml ./
COPY .mvn .mvn
RUN ./mvnw dependency:go-offline        # cached layer: deps only re-download when pom changes
COPY src src
RUN ./mvnw -q package -DskipTests

# ---- runtime stage ----
FROM eclipse-temurin:21-jre
RUN useradd -r appuser
USER appuser                            # never run as root
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=build /app/target/*.jar app.jar
EXPOSE 8080
ENTRYPOINT ["java", "-XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75.0", "-jar", "app.jar"]

talkingPoints: Multi-stage build: small final image with no JDK or source in production
Layer ordering for cache: dependencies copied before source
Non-root user and a JRE-only base image
alternatives: Spring Boot bootBuildImage (buildpacks) or Jib: no Dockerfile at all

topics.title: Docker Compose
topics.description: Wiring an app and its database together for local development.

compose.title: docker-compose.yml
compose.code:
services:
  app:
    build: .
    ports: ["8080:8080"]
    environment:
      SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL: jdbc:postgresql://db:5432/app
    depends_on: [db]
  db:
    image: postgres:16
    environment: { POSTGRES_PASSWORD: secret }
    volumes: [pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data]
volumes:
  pgdata:

notes: Services reach each other by service name through built-in DNS
For integration tests prefer Testcontainers: a real Postgres or Kafka per test run

topics.title: Kubernetes Objects
topics.description: The core object model and how the pieces stack up in a typical service.

rows: Pod
Smallest unit: usually one container plus shared network and storage; ephemeral
Deployment
Desired state for N pod replicas; rolling updates and rollback
Service
Stable virtual IP and DNS in front of pods (ClusterIP internal, NodePort and LoadBalancer external)
Ingress
L7 HTTP routing (host and path to service) plus TLS
ConfigMap / Secret
Config and credentials injected as env vars or files
HPA
Horizontal Pod Autoscaler: scales replicas on CPU, memory, or custom metrics
StatefulSet / Job / CronJob
Stateful apps with stable identity / one-off work / scheduled work
Namespace
Logical isolation for dev, staging, and teams

topics.diagram:
Ingress → Service (orders) → Deployment → Pods (3 replicas)
                                   ↑ ConfigMap + Secret mounted

topics.title: Deployment Manifest
topics.description: The Deployment fields that matter in review and in interviews.

manifest.title: deployment.yaml

keyPoints: Pin an explicit image tag, never latest in production
Requests drive scheduling; memory limits are the OOMKill threshold
Config and credentials arrive via envFrom with a ConfigMap and a Secret

topics.title: Probes
topics.description: A favourite interview question: what each probe means and how failing one differs.

probes.name: Liveness
probes.description: Restart me if this fails, for deadlock detection. Keep it dumb: do not include database checks, or a database outage restarts your whole fleet.

probes.name: Readiness
probes.description: Do not send me traffic yet, during startup, warmup, or while a dependency is down. Failing removes the pod from Service endpoints; it is not restarted.

topics.springBoot: Spring Boot exposes both liveness and readiness groups with management.endpoint.health.probes.enabled=true.

topics.title: Rollouts & Scaling
topics.description: How new versions ship and how replica counts move.

strategies.description: New pods come up gradually under maxSurge and maxUnavailable while old pods are drained. Use kubectl rollout undo to roll back.
Two full environments with traffic switched at once. Instant rollback, double the cost.
Send a small percentage to the new version, watch metrics, then ramp up. Driven by a service mesh or weighted ingress.

topics.title: kubectl Commands
topics.description: The survival set for working a live cluster.

commands.title: kubectl survival commands
commands.code:
kubectl get pods -n prod -o wide
kubectl describe pod orders-7d9f...        # events section = why it's Pending/CrashLoop
kubectl logs -f deploy/orders --previous   # logs of the crashed container
kubectl exec -it orders-7d9f... -- sh
kubectl rollout status deploy/orders
kubectl rollout undo deploy/orders
kubectl top pods                           # resource usage

topics.title: Debugging
steps: kubectl describe the pod: was it OOMKilled, a bad image, or a failing probe?
kubectl logs --previous to read the crashed container's output
Check resource limits and the liveness probe first, the two usual suspects for Java apps
Heap larger than the memory limit, or slow startup against an aggressive probe, in which case add a startupProbe

topics.title: Interview Questions
topics.description: The five questions this topic is most often tested on.

questions.question: What happens when you kubectl apply a Deployment update?
questions.answer: A new ReplicaSet is created; pods are scaled up and down per the rolling-update strategy; readiness probes gate traffic; the old ReplicaSet is kept for rollback history.

questions.question: How do containers change how you configure a Spring Boot app?
questions.answer: Externalize everything, twelve-factor style: env vars and mounted ConfigMaps override application.yml via Spring's property precedence; secrets come from Secret objects or a vault and are never baked into images; the same image is promoted through all environments.

questions.question: Why did your Java pod get OOMKilled even though the heap was fine?
questions.answer: Container memory is heap plus metaspace plus threads plus direct buffers plus native memory. The limit must cover the total: use MaxRAMPercentage rather than setting Xmx equal to the limit, and leave roughly 25 percent headroom.

questions.question: Service versus Ingress?
questions.answer: A Service is a stable L4 endpoint that load balances across pods inside the cluster. An Ingress is an L7 router mapping external hostnames and paths to Services, with TLS termination.

questions.question: How do you do zero-downtime deploys?
questions.answer: Readiness probes plus a rolling update plus graceful shutdown (server.shutdown=graceful, a preStop hook, and a termination grace period so in-flight requests finish) plus connection draining at the load balancer.
